fact: Valley with a partly dry riverbed on the eastern coast of Sifnos; U-shaped, opening to the sea; named after the monastery of Panagia Poulati (built 1865-1872); formerly called 'The Garden' (ο κήπος)
DECA: a territory of about 300,000 m2 from the outskirts of Artemonas to the coast (DECA writes 'Northwestern coast'; the monastery and the chapter place it on the east coast)
Monastery of Panagia Poulati: OSM way 401645635, 36.98404 N, 24.73667 E
Irrigated terraces and fields ~15.5 ha; still cultivated <6% (~1 ha)
9 known springs from sea level to 140 m; flow varies by season and year; water is common whatever land the spring is on
Over 30 stone tanks: about 10 troughs (γούρνες, ~3 m3) and 21 open-air cisterns (χαβούζες, 15-20 m3), of which 5 communal (near springs 1, 3, 5, 6, 7) feeding secondary cisterns below
Open storage: 21 x 15-20 m3 + ~10 x 3 m3 = about 345-450 m3
The cisterns were not covered, so everyone knew how much water was stored
Stone furrows (κουτέντο, probably from Latin contentum) link the cisterns; most replaced by plastic pipe; old furrows serve as evidence of rights in disputes
Each plot opens the outlet to its own cistern for agreed 12-hour spans ('waters') on set weekdays; e.g. one contract: four waters a week, Tuesday, Wednesday, Saturday, Sunday; others: once a week
Rights belong to the land, not the owner; written in sale and inheritance contracts from the early 20th century; plots holding a spring or communal cistern do not mention them
Overflows and drain-offs (στραγγίδια) shared by unwritten agreement: 'no water is ever lost'
In a drought, farmed plots are watered first; active farmers tacitly use the rights of abandoned plots
An elder who holds the memory of the rules acts as informal monitor; going to court is 'unthinkable'
Water time recorded on stone tiles when plot owners donated water to build the monastery (1865-1872): 'Each proprietor had his day and his hours'
Hand-built stone infrastructure ~21,000 m3; more than 30 local words for stone; the top terrace owner rebuilds a fallen wall
34 properties: 6 with summer houses, 5 farmed, 23 abandoned-looking; 14 over 0.4 ha (eligible for a building permit)
Farmers: more than 25 in the 1980s (ZEPOU24; DECA says at least 100 in the recent past); 6 in September 2022, 4 of them over 75
Unauthorised building; drilling into the springs' aquifer; the 2015 cadastre placing the main old communal cistern on private land, separated from its spring; tourism
